answer.generated: Virtual memory management and database buffer management both operate at the level of the memory hierarchy, but they serve different purposes. Virtual memory management translates logical addresses into physical addresses and handles paging or segmentation to provide a larger address space than physical memory allows. Database buffer management caches data blocks in main memory to reduce disk I/O, improving performance. Together, they interact by integrating the operating system's virtual memory system with the database's buffering strategy, allowing the OS to manage the overall memory space while the database optimizes local caching.
